transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-20
Start time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Michael Chen (Redwood SE), Aisha Rahman (Velaris Head of Data), Derek Lowe (Velaris Lead ML Eng), Priya Singh (Velaris PM), Samir Patel (Velaris Security)

Summary (auto): Quick retro on the pilot eval, focus on an uptick in false positives on the claims classifier slice, discuss guardrail tuning and next steps for a quantized canary.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Uh, quick roll call then we'll dive in. Jordan Park from Redwood — I'm here with Michael Chen, our SE.
[00:00:12] Michael: Hey all.
[00:00:14] Aisha: Aisha here.
[00:00:16] Derek: Derek — hi.
[00:00:18] Priya: Priya — thanks.
[00:00:20] Samir: Samir on security.
[00:00:23] Jordan: Great. Agenda: scorecard review, false-positive investigation, prompt set pruning, and the quantized canary proposal. Any other items?
[00:00:34] Aisha: No, that covers it. We're mostly worried about the FP spike on the third-party claims slice.
[00:00:40] Jordan: Okay let's pull up the slide... (murmur) Michael, do you want to lead the scorecard walkthrough?
[00:00:46] Michael: Sure. So on slide 3 we show daily precision/recall for the main classifiers. You'll see overall precision is steady at ~0.88, recall 0.85, but the third-party claims slice dropped precision from 0.82 to 0.67 over the last seven days.
[00:01:05] Derek: Right, and that aligns with what we saw in production — more false positives flagged by the rules engine.
[00:01:12] Michael: We did a slice breakdown — the drop seems correlated with prompts that include multi-claim descriptions and scanned documents. The KV cash cache — sorry, KV cache warm path — it's not likely the root cause but it affects latency.
[00:01:29] Aisha: There were a couple of prompt edits last week, we added a shorter-context template for speed. Could that have increased FPs?
[00:01:37] Michael: Possibly — shorter context can drop disambiguating tokens. I ran a small A/B on the prompt variants and saw a 4% delta.
[00:01:45] Priya: What's the scoring threshold right now for the auto-accept path?
[00:01:49] Jordan: It's at 0.78. Priya, I think you suggested revisiting thresholds?
[00:01:56] Priya: Yeah, given the slice behavior maybe bump to 0.82 for that slice, but we worry about throughput.
[00:02:04] Michael: Bumping thresholds will reduce FPs but increase manual review load. There's a cost/latency tradeoff. We also proposed a quantized variant which lowers latency and cost but might increase small hallucinations.
[00:02:18] Aisha: Can you explain the quantized model tradeoffs in plain terms again?
[00:02:22] Michael: Yeah. Quantization reduces model size — lower memory footprint, faster tokens, cheaper per-token cost. The downside can be a small drop in generation quality, especially on edge cases. For this workload we saw a median latency drop of ~18% and a cost drop ~30% in Redwood's bench, with model accuracy delta around -1.8% on our eval set.
[00:02:43] Derek: Important to know which failure modes widen — is it more hallucination or more subtle mislabels?
[00:02:48] Michael: Mostly borderline token choices, which sometimes pushes a borderline 'no' to 'yes'. That's why guardrails matter.
[00:02:54] Jordan: Let's jump into the regression that Aisha flagged. Michael, can you show the top failing prompts?
[00:02:58] Michael: Yep. I'm sharing a CSV with the top 120 failing prompts. Example — prompt ID 572: long multi-claim narrative, lots of date ranges. Original model handled it, but our recent prompt pruning removed some clarifying lead-in text. So there's a human prompt-crafting regression.
[00:03:20] Aisha: Ah, so the editing of templates to shorten context is a likely contributor. I own that change, I can revert or create a special template for multi-claim docs.
[00:03:29] Priya: Can we batch by template type so multi-claim gets longer context and others get short?
[00:03:33] Michael: Yes, Redwood supports per-route prompt templates and automatic batching by template. Batching more similar prompts also helps token efficiency.
[00:03:41] Samir: Quick security question — if we move to quantized in a canary, where does the model run? On Redwood Dedicated or in our VPC?
[00:03:49] Jordan: For the pilot we suggested running the canary on Redwood Dedicated in us-west with VPC peering. If you want on-prem or Private, that's an option but adds setup time.
[00:03:59] Samir: We need KMS integration and audit logs regardless. Also, encryption at rest for KV cache and model artifacts.
[00:04:07] Michael: Yep, Redwood Private and Dedicated both support KMS and audit hooks — we'll share the security brief.
[00:04:12] Aisha: Back to the FP spike — are there any signal-level fixes short-term?
[00:04:16] Michael: Short-term we can: 1) tweak threshold for the slice; 2) add a secondary classifier that targets multi-claim hallucination; 3) revert the short-template for those prompts. Long-term, more diverse promps in eval and a guardrail reranker.
[00:04:31] Derek: How expensive is the secondary classifier? Is that an extra endpoint call?
[00:04:35] Michael: Could be implemented as a lightweight reranker — smaller model, cheap relative to full gen, called only on borderline scores. It adds latency only for borderline cases.
[00:04:44] Priya: That might be a nice middle ground. Can we simulate the cost/latency tradeoff?
[00:04:48] Michael: Yes, I can run a simulated traffic sweep — take 10k real prompts, apply the reranker to borderline 8% of cases, and show the added latency and cost delta.
[00:04:57] Aisha: That would be helpful. Also, I can provide a labeled set of top-200 problem prompts.
[00:05:02] Jordan: Cool. Let's talk about the quantized canary plan — timeline and rollback. Michael?
[00:05:07] Michael: Proposed plan: spin up quantized variant behind a rollout policy — 5% canary traffic for 48 hours, monitor FP rate and manual review backlog. If FP exceeds +3% relative to baseline or manual backlog grows > 12/hr, auto-rollback.
[00:05:22] Derek: The auto-rollback hook — how fast is it?
[00:05:25] Michael: It can revert within 60–90 seconds. It's implemented via routing policy in Redwood, plus automatic model fallbacks.
[00:05:31] Priya: Do we have observability for token-level cost breakdown and per-route latency?
[00:05:36] Jordan: Yes, Redwood Console will give per-route latency, token counts, and cost cadence. We'll give you a dashboard link.
[00:05:41] Samir: Audit logs for routing changes and who triggered rollbacks are required for our compliance team.
[00:05:46] Jordan: Yes, those are part of the Dedicated audit features — all routing and model changes are logged with actor and timestamp.
[00:05:51] Aisha: One more thing: the scoring script in our pipeline changed last week — Derek — you pushed a new tokenizer preproc?
[00:05:57] Derek: I tweaked whitespace normalization to remove OCR artifacts. Might have impacted tokens for scanned docs. Good catch.
[00:06:03] Aisha: Okay so we have three vectors: prompt template edits, tokenizer change, and model variant effects. All could contribute. We need an experiment plan to isolate.
[00:06:12] Michael: Proposed experiment: run a 1k-prompt batch on the current baseline, the quantized variant, and the baseline with reverted template + original tokenizer. Compare precision/recall and latency/cost.
[00:06:24] Jordan: That maps to an action item. Michael — can you run that and upload the heatmap and CSV?
[00:06:29] Michael: Yep — target by next Tue 2025-05-27.
[00:06:33] Priya: For thresholds, I want to tentatively set target success criteria: F1 >= 0.84 and false positives < 2% on the top-200 prompts. Priya again.
[00:06:43] Jordan: Noted. We'll use those for canary gating.
[00:06:46] Aisha: Security: Samir, any blockers on KMS?
[00:06:50] Samir: We need Redwood's SOC2 artifact and KMS key rotation policy. Also want to vet the peering config. I can do that review but need the docs.
[00:06:58] Jordan: I'll drop the security brief and KMS spec after this call.
[00:07:02] Michael: Quick note — quantized model requires different kernel selection and some GPUs handle int8 better. If we run on dedicated pools we can pick nodes optimized for int8. That's in the runbook.
[00:07:14] Derek: Which hardware are you recommending?
[00:07:16] Michael: A100s with specific int8 kernels or newer H100 if available; we'll include options and cost impact in the pricing.
[00:07:24] Priya: Can we try a staged template revert just for the failing prompts? So we don't impact global latency.
[00:07:29] Michael: Yes, route-by-template is supported. We can create a special route that uses the long-context template for multi-claim and keep short template for others.
[00:07:38] Aisha: I'll flag the multi-claim prompts in our prompt set and share them by Friday.
[00:07:42] Jordan: Excellent. Any other blockers?
[00:07:45] Priya: One ask — if quantization shows a small drop in accuracy but saves 30% cost, can we pilot a hybrid approach where cost-sensitive traffic uses quantized and sensitive slices use full precision?
[00:07:58] Michael: Absolutely, that's a common pattern — cost/risk routing. Redwood supports policy-based routing so you can pick model variant per slice.
[00:08:06] Aisha: That seems ideal.
[00:08:08] Jordan: Okay let's capture next steps.
[00:08:11] Michael: Action: run 1k-prompt batch across three variants (baseline, baseline+revert, quantized) and share heatmap by 2025-05-27.
[00:08:20] Jordan: Action: send security brief, KMS spec, and pricing by 2025-05-23.
[00:08:25] Aisha: Action: share top-200 problem prompts and label set by 2025-05-22.
[00:08:31] Priya: I'll confirm success criteria and manual review capacity numbers by 2025-05-25.
[00:08:35] Samir: I'll start the security review; expecting follow-up Qs.
[00:08:39] Jordan: Great. Any quick questions before we close?
[00:08:43] Derek: No, sounds good.
[00:08:45] Aisha: No. Thanks.
[00:08:47] Jordan: Thanks everyone — we'll regroup after the heatmap.
[00:53:30] Jordan: (wrap) End call.
